gap: No result ChatGPT got states that at the makers' own US stores today the TerraMaster F2-425 Plus ($399.49) costs only $9.50 more than the UGREEN DXP2800 ($389.99), nor that Synology confirmed it removed the i915 graphics driver from the J4125 DS225+/DS425+, which disables Plex hardware transcoding on the model NAS Decoded recommends for it.
standout_why: Starry Hope lists the DXP2800 at $389.99 but never prices the F2-425 Plus, and lists the F4-425 Plus at $599–649. NAS Decoded prices only the DS225+ ('about $360', undated) and claims its iGPU handles Plex hardware transcoding, with no mention of the driver removal. Terabytewise and Datacenterdisk price from Amazon ($389.99 DXP2800, $487.99 TS-264) with no TerraMaster F2-425 Plus or F4-425 price and no Synology driver note. ChatGPT's answer rests on a $296.99 Walmart price for the DXP2800 that I could not open (Walmart served a bot wall); the maker store is $93 higher, which erases the price gap that made the DXP2800 its pick.
decides: At maker-store prices the F2-425 Plus (Intel N150, 8 GB DDR5 to 32 GB, 3× NVMe, 2× 5GbE, native Plex app) and the DXP2800 (N100, 8 GB to 16 GB, 2× NVMe, 1× 2.5GbE, Plex only via Docker with a device bind mount) are within $10 of each other, so the F2-425 Plus becomes the pick unless the shopper can actually buy the DXP2800 near $297. The Synology DS225+/DS425+ are excluded outright: the maker shipped them without the graphics driver Plex needs. Everything else under $500 either has 4 GB RAM and no stated CPU model (F2-425, F4-425), is out of stock (F2-424), lacks Quick Sync (DH2300, DH4300 Plus), or has no maker or retailer price under $500 that I could open (TS-264, AS5402T, DS224+, F2-423).

findings.value: i915 graphics driver removed from DSM; hardware transcoding disabled on the J4125
findings.source_title: Get Graphics Drivers and Hardware Transcoding BACK for Plex/Jellyfin/Emby on your Synology NAS – NAS Compares
findings.note: Article dated 24 Sep 2025 names the DS225+ and DS425+. Quote: 'Synology had removed the i915 graphics driver from DSM'; 'Synology confirmed the change in support tickets', citing HEVC licensing costs. The workaround 'can cause instability, break after DSM updates' and 'requires maintenance after reboots'. Applies equally to the DS425+. The DS224+ is not named in the article.

findings.label: Plex hardware transcoding rules
findings.value: Plex Pass required; no artificial limit on simultaneous Intel streams; Jasper Lake or newer needed for reliable HEVC output; Docker needs a device bind mount
findings.note: Quotes: 'requires an active Plex Pass subscription'; Intel on Linux/Windows devices 'do not have any artificial limit to the number of simultaneous videos'; NAS users 'will require JasperLake or better CPU to reliably transcode to HEVC output'; 'Compatible TerraMaster NAS devices require Plex Media Server 1.13.9 or newer'; Docker bind mount is 'an advanced setup'. Contradicts ChatGPT's 2–4 stream table being a hardware cap.
